rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-3.3, Figs 3-8, Tables 3-4 - the authors run their own ISAREG water-balance simulations for four irrigation scheduling alternatives over 1970-1992 and for pessimistic/optimistic precipitation scenarios at the Pustren vertisol site, reporting irrigation demand, ASW and relative yield decrease.
rows.notes: The study is a pure simulation exercise: it uses the ISAREG model (FAO56-based) to compare three furrow irrigation scheduling alternatives and a rainfed option for two maize hybrids under present climate and hypothetical 2005-2030 rainfall scenarios, concluding that all alternatives can accommodate foreseen changes, alternative 2 (MAD 0.33) gives least yield impact, alternative 3 saves most water in average years, and stress-sensitive hybrids should be avoided under deficit/rainfed conditions. Model calibration and validation (Kc, p, Ky) are cited from a former study (Popova et al., 2006a); in this paper no simulation output is compared with measurements from the real system, and the only comparison is with regionally advised schedules (Zahariev et al., 1986), not observations. Under the rubric a model never checked against observations within the study is not own evidence on the claimed effect, so Q2 is no. Even if Q2 were accepted: single site/soil (one vertisol), plot/field scale, no replication-based dispersion (only an 80% CI of ETo climate means), authors note the precipitation trend cannot be interpreted as a real trend and that results do not allow selecting a best alternative; they state a vertisol-specific condition (soil moisture above cracking threshold, MAD constrained) that derives from earlier cited experiments rather than this study.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a modelling/scenario analysis with no new field measurements; all empirical calibration is from prior cited work.
